newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank very worried over Bulgarian economy.
newsitem.headline: World Bank very worried over Bulgarian economy.

text.p: The World Bank said on Tuesday it was extremely concerned about Bulgaria's deteriorating economy and was ready to support the implementation of a viable structural reform programme to boost long-term growth.
"The World Bank continues to monitor the progress of a government programme which aims to reform the state-owned enterprise sector," the bank said in a statement.

Under an agreement signed last year the first phase of reforms comprises privatising 25 percent of state-owned enterprise assets, closing or selling off 64 large loss-making state enterprises and isolating from lending a further 71 enterprises, it said.
Bulgaria stands to receive $100 million in budgetary support on completion of these reform targets, under an Enterprise Sector Adjustment Loan (ESAL).

"The World Bank has already extended a $30 million Rehabilitation Loan to strengthen the social safety net by financing enhanced severance benefits to employees whose jobs were affected by the closures," the bank said.
The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have suspended funding because of the Socialist government's failure to reduce budget-draining subsidies and boost revenue through sell-offs.

In November the IMF proposed the introduction of a currency board system, which would severely curb the financial powers of the government and the central bank, to boost confidence in the crumbling financial system.

However growing political unrest and pressure on the ruling Socialist party, composed largely of ex-communists, to hold early elections half way through its term, will delay implementation of reforms. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
